newsitem.title: USA: IMF happy at Lithuanian growth, seeks bank reform.
newsitem.headline: IMF happy at Lithuanian growth, seeks bank reform.

text.p: Lithuania has done well to cut inflation and stimulate economic growth, but needs to boost domestic savings and tackle problems in the banking system, the International Monetary Fund said on Monday.
A summary of the IMF's annual assessment of the Lithuanian economy said that higher farm output was the main factor behind recent economic growth.

It said agricultural reforms planned for 1997 would make the sector more transparent and noted that privatization would be accelerated through international tenders for larger companies. But more still had to be done.
"Directors commended Lithuania for the considerable progress made in reducing inflation and in attaining strong growth," the IMF said.

"Directors nonetheless stressed that in the period ahead...further efforts would be needed to increase domestic savings, speedily resolve problems in the banking system and deepen structural reforms, particularly in the areas of privatization, agriculture and social security provision."

The IMF praised Lithuanian central bank efforts to deal with private banks which did not meet prudential requirements but described the completed restructuring of the Lithuanian banking system as "an urgent task".
It said further structural reforms were needed to accelerate growth and said the government should take a bolder approach to the sale of state holdings.
Lithuanian GDP rose 3.6 percent last year, after growth of three percent in 1995. Year-end inflation fell to 13.1 percent from 35.5 percent at the end of 1995.
